headline: Redpine said six more publishers have licensed their research papers to AI agents, bringing more than 20 million articles under paid access.
score_reason: Useful licensing step for AI research tools; results are company-reported.
importance_line: Researchers and developers building AI assistants could get traceable, licensed access to full papers and publishers get paid per use, but the accuracy gain is Redpine's own test and it is unclear whether authors receive anything directly.
summary: Unite.AI reports that Redpine, a Swedish company, announced on 6 October 2026 that publishers including BMJ Group, Sage and IOP Publishing joined its partnerships covering more than 20 million peer-reviewed articles, which AI agents can use for a fee through an API and the Model Context Protocol. In Redpine's own test on 179 biomedical questions, an agent using its service scored 84.7 against 75.9 without it.
notes: Company announcement relayed by Unite.AI. Category MKT chosen: the news is a licensing deal; use RES if the desk prefers science tooling.
